upstream_provenance.verificationMethod: Proterial 'MaDC-F' catalogue PR-EM13 (2022-12), ML91S data sheet, sheet pages 07-08 (PDF page 5), test core toroid OD 14 mm, ID 7 mm, HT 5 mm, sha256 cd4bf78e...537c. The sheet prints the core loss formula Pcv[kW/m3] = k Bm^a f^b (Bm in T, f in Hz) for 500-1000 kHz and 1000-3000 kHz at 23 C and 100 C: 500-1000 kHz 23 C k 6.490E-06 a 3.335 b 1.938, 100 C k 2.022E-07 a 3.553 b 2.241; 1000-3000 kHz 23 C k 4.109E-10 a 2.929 b 2.533, 100 C k 2.067E-11 a 3.077 b 2.784. k, alpha (f exponent), beta (B exponent) of each range are the 23 C formula (k x 1000 to W/m3, divided by ct(23 C) = 1.0196). The formulas and the measured markers drawn beside them cover Bm 20-50 mT and 23 C and 100 C only; the sheet's design notice says Bm less than 50 mT. Outside 20-50 mT, 23-100 C and 500 kHz-3 MHz the model is not backed by the sheet. ct(T): ct(23 C) fixed by the kept k; ct(100 C) = the least-squares (log) ratio of the 100 C to the 23 C formula over each range's frequencies x 20-50 mT (500 kHz-1 MHz: 0.880, the ratio itself spans 0.71-1.07; 1-3 MHz: 1.120, spanning 0.90-1.36); the curvature, which two temperatures cannot fix, from the sheet's 'Temperature dependence of core loss' figure (1 MHz/50 mT curve for 500 kHz-1 MHz, 2 MHz/50 mT curve for 1-3 MHz, drawn 20-120 C), its linear part removed. Against the 100 C formula: rms 9.6 % (500 kHz-1 MHz) and 10.0 % (1-3 MHz); against the measured markers at 23 and 100 C: rms 13.1 % and 16.2 %. Residuals of the sheet itself: the table's 2 MHz/50 mT/100 C value is 700 kW/m3 while the 2 MHz 100 C markers read 599 kW/m3; the 1 MHz/50 mT loss-temperature curve reads 91 kW/m3 at 23 C while the 1 MHz 23 C markers read 113 kW/m3 and the formula gives 126 kW/m3. recommendations.maximumMagneticFluxDensity 0.05 T is the sheet's design notice: 'Transformer or Inductor using ML91S shall be designed under the condition of magnetic flux density, Bm, less than 50mT.'
